why: A race witness names the statement of the first difference on each side (design/race-lines.md). Slot.claim re-checks its turn after the await and an overtaken caller returns -1; the candidate drops the check, so the requests agree in every order and the first call whose outcome differs gives the two return statements: the parent's `return -1` against the candidate's `return this.count`. Slot.publish guards a request to the outside with the same check; the candidate drops it, so the requests differ and the witness names the statement that made each side's first differing request. Slot.tally keeps the check and adds a local for the new count: a pure refactor, PASS-bounded with its order count, no race read into it. Slot.label is untouched. Lane A refuses nothing here by choice but is not the point: the race is lane B's alone (laneBOnly).
